title: Luxor
standfirst: Luxor stands on the site of ancient Thebes, with temples on the East Bank and the royal tombs on the West Bank. Most Nile cruises start or end here. It is one of the stops in our guide to [[up]].

sections.heading: The East Bank
paragraphs: Karnak, the largest temple complex of ancient Egypt, and Luxor Temple, in the middle of the modern town and lit after dark. Most cruises visit both on the first or last day.

sections.heading: The West Bank
paragraphs: The Valley of the Kings, where the pharaohs of the New Kingdom were buried, the terraced temple of Hatshepsut at Deir el-Bahari and the Colossi of Memnon. Visits start early, before the heat.

sections.heading: Time in Luxor
paragraphs: A cruise covers the main sites. Many travellers add a night before or after for the museums, more tombs or a balloon flight over the West Bank at sunrise.

faqs.q: How long do I need in Luxor?
faqs.a: A cruise covers the main sites in one or two days. Add a night for a slower pace or more tombs.

faqs.q: Is the tomb of Tutankhamun included?
faqs.a: Usually not: it needs a separate ticket, like a few other tombs in the Valley of the Kings.

seoTitle: Luxor on a Nile cruise: temples and tombs
seoDescription: Luxor on a Nile cruise: Karnak and Luxor Temple on the East Bank, the Valley of the Kings and Hatshepsut's temple on the West Bank.
